commit.message:
fix(ci): report advisories on unchanged dependencies without blocking unrelated changes (#580)

## What

Only advisories against dependency versions newly introduced by a change
fail the required audit; existing advisories remain visible without
blocking unrelated changes or releases. License, ban, source,
yanked-crate and unused-dependency violations still block.

The full report appears as a non-required `advisories` status on
same-repository PRs, in lint’s summary and log on every PR, and as an
independent job on `main`. It audits the checked-out merge result, so
advisories already fixed on the base disappear from the report. A
committed check contract and regression tests keep reporting
informational and PR CI at four jobs.

## Why

RUSTSEC-2026-0433 against pulldown-cmark blocked every change and forced
a manual release merge, even though this crate did not enable the
affected feature. Managers need outstanding advisories to stay visible
across their work without advisory database updates blocking unrelated
changes and releases.

## Additional info

The PR report runs even after earlier lint steps fail, and its result
never fails lint. Fork PRs receive the summary and log without a commit
status because their tokens cannot post one. No job depends on the
advisory report, and no advisory is ignored or downgraded in
configuration.

Branch protection reconciliation remains a follow-up: `lint`,
`test-linux`, `test-windows` and `test-macos` stay required;
`advisories` must never be required.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nick DeRobertis <19440155+nickderobertis@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix(test): stop the e2e fixture server's port race and a Windows live-test timeout (#581)

## What

Fixes three causes of flaky tests. Each has a regression test that
drives its cause on purpose instead of waiting for a slow host, and
fails with the fix removed:

| Flaky test | Cause | Fix | Regression evidence | Base failure evidence
|
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Browser fixture server port race (`apps/dag-ui-e2e`) |
`startFixtureServer` picked a port by opening a probe, closing it and
binding the port seconds later. Anything else could take it in between;
a restart likewise gave the port up between servers. | The read API
binds `127.0.0.1:0` and announces the port it took. `startFixtureServer`
keeps holding that port through restarts and relays connections to
whichever server is current. `--origin-port` makes the fixture data link
to that held port. | `fixture-server.spec.ts`: both journeys squat every
port a probe or restart releases, at the moment it is released. Both
fail with the base `fixture-server.ts`/`serve-fixture.mjs` and pass with
the fix. `dag-ui.spec.ts` holds `serve-fixture.mjs` to refusing `--port
0` without `--origin-port`. | Actions run 41410850207, test-linux job
125163321641: the fixture server exited 2 on `Address already in use`. |
| Windows
`live::a_cursor_older_than_the_retained_frames_is_answered_stale`
timeout | The poller held the sidebar lock for an entire read of the
runs directory, including slow summary-cache writes on Windows, and `GET
/api/v2/events` waited on that lock. | `src/live.rs` reads runs without
the sidebar lock and takes only the brief lock needed to store what it
read. | `tests/e2e/live.rs`
`a_stream_and_a_subscription_are_answered_while_the_sidebar_is_reading_a_run`
blocks a run's summary read on a FIFO, so the read stalls for as long as
the test holds it, and requires streams and subscriptions to answer
meanwhile. Fails with the base `src/live.rs`, passes with the fix. |
Actions run 41410850207, cross (windows-latest) job 125163458376. |
| Stop-button header journey (`dag-ui-header.spec.ts` "Stop is offered
only before a run has ended") | A run written after the poller's last
look was missing from a subscription's own snapshot, so the browser took
it for unserved and opened a different run. | A subscription reads its
run's row when the sidebar lacks it, includes it in the snapshot, and
sends it to existing subscriptions. | `tests/e2e/live.rs`
`a_run_no_look_has_listed_yet_is_in_the_snapshot_of_a_subscription_to_it`
subscribes to a run no look has listed. Fails with the base
`src/live.rs`, passes with the fix. | No CI record found among recent
failed runs, and the journey passed 10/10 locally against the base
server. The evidence is the regression test above failing on the base,
plus the earlier local observation that the journey failed about half
the time. |

## Not in this change

Two other intermittent journeys are left identical to the base and
recorded as follow-ups:

- **Long-body human-item detail** (`dag-ui-human-items.spec.ts`): the
attempted fix still depended on Chromium's animated keyboard scroll,
which reduced-motion emulation does not turn off. No CI failure of this
cause was found, and the journey passed 20/20 locally on the base.
- **Dropped-stream resume** (`dag-ui-live-updates.spec.ts`): failed in
Actions run 41447098814 (test-linux job 125282831903) at line 662,
`after` ≠ `lastFrame`. The attempted fix's forced frame proved only half
of it: removing the wait for the browser's drop report still passed.

## Verification

- Browser journeys in `fixture-server`, `dag-ui`, `dag-ui-header`,
`dag-ui-live-updates` and `dag-ui-human-items`: 124 passed.
- e2e `live` suite: 25 passed.
- `just fmt-check`, `just lint`, `just lint-llm-validate` and `just
lint-llm-diff` pass.

No test is skipped, retried, or given a longer timeout, and no existing
assertion is weakened.

## Why

Unrelated CI failures blocked a three-line packaging comment three times
and forced a manual merge. Ordinary changes should not stall because
another process takes a fixture's port or slow storage stops the live
API from answering.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
